fit: Parkinson clinical review with medication-related visual history
assessment: The review describes reported visual hallucinations as part of psychosis and discusses different medication contexts. It does not measure a new clinical comparison, a visual episode rate, or dried-fig exposure.

fit: Parkinson perfusion and visual reasoning comparison
assessment: The study compared 28 nondemented Parkinson participants with 17 controls. It correlated right visual-association-area perfusion with a visual reasoning score. The abstract reports no separately coded visual event frequency or measured fig exposure.

The 601 assessed participants included 20 probable and 10 possible dementia with Lewy bodies cases. A diagnostic prevalence is not a within-person visual event rate. Full symptom coding remains pending.

fit: Uncontrolled dementia follow-up, Parkinson subgroup of three
assessment: Behavioral ratings improved over follow-up in the Parkinson dementia subgroup. The published 45% visual figure has no compatible affected-patient numerator at the recorded subgroup size of three. This is a drug follow-up without a separately enumerated visual episode rate or dried figs.
The differential table describes visual hallucinations as a feature of one dementia phenotype. The review has no original visual-frequency or dried-fig comparison.

fit: Parkinson perfusion grouped by dementia status
assessment: Thirty participants with Parkinson dementia and 22 without dementia were compared with 10 controls. The result concerns occipital perfusion and cognitive scores. It does not report counted visual episodes or a fig comparison.
